x: B is the odd one out: orthodox Muslims rejected Mirza Ghulam Ahmad's claim to be a messiah, so the movement never accepted their objections. A liberal and universal religion, opposition to jihad and Western liberal education among Muslims were all Ahmadiya features.

The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule at Pune in 1873. The others are mismatched: the Arya Samaj was founded at Bombay in 1875, the Prarthana Samaj at Bombay in 1867, and the Paramahansa Mandali at Bombay (not Calcutta) in 1849.

Baba Dayal Das founded the Nirankari movement (UPSC dates it to 1855), which worshipped God as Nirankar, the formless. Baba Ram Singh led the Kukas, Kartar Singh Jhabbar the Akalis, and Shiv Dayal Singh founded the Radhasoami Satsang.

B is correct: the Justice Party opposed both the freedom struggle and the Andhra movement, which, along with Andhra-Tamil rivalry, cost it support. Option C is the reverse of the truth, since it had no mass base in Andhra.
